BRAIN_ABSCESS.title: Brain abscess (pus pocket in the brain)

items: A brain abscess is a pocket of pus in the brain caused by infection.
It needs antibiotics straight away and often needs drainage.
Headache, which is usually dull and gets worse over time. It is the most common symptom.
Fever, which may be absent.
Weakness on one side, seizures (fits), or a change in alertness.
Contrast CT or MRI scan of the brain.
A sample of the pus, taken by needle or surgery, for culture.
Blood cultures, and an echocardiogram (heart ultrasound) if the infection may have spread from the heart.
An HIV test if there are risk factors.
Antibiotics are started quickly, often before the cause is known.
Drainage of the abscess may be needed. Your team will decide this.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Do not wait at home for symptoms to settle. A brain abscess needs hospital care.
Bring someone with you to hospital if you feel unwell.
Repeat scans are often needed to check the abscess is healing.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Headache that is getting worse, with fever or vomiting
Seizure, confusion, drowsiness, or new weakness

DYSENTERY.title: Dysentery (bloody diarrhoea from infection)

items: Dysentery is diarrhoea with blood or mucus, caused by germs that invade the bowel wall.
Common causes include Shigella and amoeba.
Diarrhoea with blood or mucus, and belly cramps.
Tenesmus (a painful urge to pass stool with little coming out).
Fever, which is often high with bacterial causes.
Stool culture and stool microscopy, which are sent routinely.
Blood count and kidney function tests.
Your doctor will choose antibiotics based on the stool result.
Treatment depends on the germ found.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Drink fluids to avoid dehydration.
Wash hands well and do not prepare food for others while unwell.
Tell your doctor if the blood or diarrhoea does not settle.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Signs of dehydration: little urine, dizziness, or dry mouth
Severe belly pain, or a swollen belly

items: Encephalitis is swelling of the brain, usually from a virus or other infection.
It can change alertness, behaviour, and movement.
Fever, confusion or drowsiness that lasts more than 24 hours, and fits (seizures).
New weakness or a problem on one side of the body, and a stiff neck in some people.
Lumbar puncture (fluid test) with PCR for herpes and other viruses.
MRI scan of the brain and an EEG (brain wave test).
Blood tests for regional viruses where these are common.
Your team will start treatment for the likely causes while tests are pending.
Antiviral treatment is started where indicated, based on the tests.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Do not wait at home. Encephalitis needs hospital care.
Your team will review your progress after treatment.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

ERYSIPELAS.title: Erysipelas (bright red skin infection)

items: Erysipelas is a superficial skin infection with a sharp, raised edge.
It is usually caused by a strep germ.
A bright red, raised, firm patch with a clear, raised border.
Fever, chills, and feeling unwell. Often on the legs or face.
Usually no tests are needed.
Blood cultures if you are unwell.
Your doctor will choose antibiotics based on how unwell you are.
Ask your doctor about the course length.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Raise the affected limb, and rest.
Mark the edge of the redness to see if it spreads.
See your doctor if the redness spreads or you are not better after a few days.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Redness spreading fast, or dark or blistered skin
Fever with feeling faint or confused
Severe pain or swelling that is getting worse
